verdict.rationale: Asana documents context-preserving handoffs. AI Teammates share memory so no one repeats context they have already given, and agents draw context from the Work Graph. The official MCP server brings that work graph into external AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT, and two-way sync integrations keep tools aligned. All of this is vendor marketing or docs, though, and no explicit agent-to-agent or tool-to-tool handoff protocol is described. missing for 10: a documented explicit handoff mechanism between agents or tools that guarantees context and information are preserved, details on what context transfers and its limits, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can hand off work between tools or agents without losing context or information

citations.quote: Shared memory means AI Teammates learn from the work itself. Every completed task, every piece of feedback, every preference gets carried forward, so no one repeats context they've already given
Pre-built AI agents that work alongside your team inside real workflows, with shared memory, governance, and context from the Work Graph
The Asana app in Claude brings your work graph directly into Claude conversations, allowing you to turn AI-powered discussions into actionable work without leaving Claude.
Keep teams aligned with automated one-way or two-way data synchronization — without manual updates or switching tools.
Automatically create PagerDuty incidents with context from Asana tasks using Rules.
